ops.title: Flaky under load: TestCloseContextDeadlineBoundsPinSettlementWait (native closes before callback settlement = 0, want 1)
ops.description:
mountmux/runtime_test.go:778 fails intermittently with `native closes before callback settlement = 0, want 1`. The test arms a 1ms `context.WithTimeout`, launches `runtime.CloseContext(ctx)` on a goroutine, spins until `runtime.closing`, waits `<-ctx.Done()`, then asserts the native close already landed — on a loaded macOS runner the close path can miss that 1ms window, so `native.counts()` still reads 0 closes when the assertion fires.

Proven pre-existing and unrelated to the commit that surfaced it (2026-07-26, helper-plist fix wave): first seen on the fuse-macos job of CI run 30204123984 (commit b917ec3, fusekit v1.15.4), whose only changes were CHANGELOG.md plus holder/plan.go and holder/plan_test.go — and mountmux has no import of fusekit/holder. The same fuse-macos job was green on each of the 8 preceding CI runs on main. A `gh run rerun 30204123984 --failed` then passed the job clean with no code change, confirming the flake; the run finished green and the release proceeded from b917ec3.

Fix is a design call on the deadline the test arms — a 1ms window is too tight to assert close-ordering against on a shared runner — not a blind timeout bump. Sibling of 6f39134 (the holder readiness flake from the same wave).
